title: Prompt in, text out
objective: See what one call to a language model can and can't do: it turns text into text, with no fresh facts, no actions and no memory of its own.

sources.title: Claude Platform docs: Using the Messages API ("The Messages API is stateless, which means that you always send the full conversational history")
Claude Platform docs: Models overview (each model's "reliable knowledge cutoff": the date through which its knowledge is most extensive and reliable)
Anthropic: Building effective agents ("The basic building block of agentic systems is an LLM enhanced with augmentations such as retrieval, tools, and memory")

simplifies: A real call also carries a system prompt and settings, and can include images. What a model knows depends on the model; check its documented knowledge cutoff.

steps.caption: One call: your app sends text (the prompt) and gets text back. That's all a single call does.
The model answers from what it learned in training. Each model has a documented knowledge cutoff: the date through which its knowledge is most reliable.

predict.prompt: With no tools, you ask a model for last night's match score. What do you get?

options.text: The right score: models are connected to the internet
options.explanation: A plain call has no internet access; it only sees your prompt.

options.text: It can't know: the match is after what it learned, so it should say so, or it may guess
options.explanation: Right. Fresh facts have to be put in the prompt, or fetched with a tool.
The call succeeds; the problem is what the model can know.

steps.caption: It can't act. If the text says "I've emailed Bob", no email was sent. Only your app can do things in the world.

predict.prompt: The model's reply says "Done, I've booked your table." Was a table booked?

options.explanation: A model call returns text; it can't reach a booking system.

options.text: No, unless your app did it: the model only produced text
options.explanation: Right. Actions need tools that your code runs (the next lesson).

options.text: Yes, if the reply is polite enough
options.explanation: Wording changes nothing outside the reply.

steps.caption: It has no memory between calls. The API is stateless: your app sends the whole conversation every time.

predict.prompt: Call 1 says "My name is Ravi." Call 2 asks "What's my name?" and doesn't include call 1. What happens?

options.text: It answers Ravi: models remember users
options.explanation: Each call stands alone; only what you send is seen.

options.text: The model can't know: call 2 contains no name
options.explanation: Right. Memory is your app's job: it resends the history.
The call is fine; it just has nothing to go on.

steps.caption: So your app does the remembering, and the history it resends grows with every turn: longer conversations cost more, up to the model's context limit.
What one call is good at: anything where the prompt holds everything needed, such as summarising, rewriting, classifying or drafting. Agents add retrieval, tools and memory around it.

quiz.prompt: Which task can one plain model call do well on its own?

options.explanation: That's a fresh fact; it needs a tool or the data in the prompt.
That's an action; only your app can do it.

options.text: Summarise a report you paste into the prompt
options.explanation: Right. Everything it needs is in the prompt.

quiz.prompt: Why does a chat app send the whole conversation with every message?

options.explanation: Longer prompts are slower and cost more, not less.

options.text: The API is stateless: the model only sees what is in this call
options.explanation: Right. The app keeps the history and resends it.

options.text: Because the model asks for it
options.explanation: It's how the API works, not a request from the model.
